learningObjectives.title: Religious and non-religious worldviews (including humanism and atheism)
Responses to ethical and philosophical questions

questions.q: Which of the following best describes atheism?
options: The belief that God's existence cannot be known
The belief that there is no God or gods
The belief in one supreme God
questions.explain: Atheism is the position that no God or gods exist.

questions.q: What does agnosticism claim?
options: The existence of God can be proven by science
It is not possible to know whether God exists
questions.explain: Agnosticism holds that the existence of God is unknown or unknowable.

questions.q: The term 'theism' refers to the...
options: belief in the existence of God or gods
separation of religion and the state
questions.explain: Theism is belief in the existence of a God or gods.

questions.q: Humanism is a non-religious worldview that bases its approach to life primarily on...
options: the teachings of a single prophet
tradition handed down by a church
questions.explain: Humanism relies on reason, evidence and human experience rather than the supernatural.

questions.q: According to Humanists, where does morality come from?
options: from God's commands revealed in holy books
from human empathy, reason and concern for others' welfare
from the laws of a church
questions.explain: Humanists ground ethics in human empathy and reason, not in divine command.

questions.q: Secularism is best defined as the principle that...
options: religion and the state should be kept separate
everyone should follow the same religion
questions.explain: Secularism holds that religion and the state should remain separate.

questions.q: Humanists UK was known by which name before it was renamed in 2017?
questions.explain: The British Humanist Association was renamed Humanists UK in 2017.

questions.q: What is the main difference between atheism and humanism?
options: Atheism is a religion whereas humanism is not
Atheism is simply the absence of belief in God, while humanism is a positive worldview with values about how to live
Humanism requires belief in an afterlife
There is no difference between them
questions.explain: Atheism only denies God's existence, whereas humanism adds a positive framework of values.

questions.q: Whose theory of evolution by natural selection, published in 1859, offered a non-religious explanation for the diversity of life?
questions.explain: Charles Darwin set out evolution by natural selection in On the Origin of Species (1859).

questions.q: 'Inter-faith dialogue' refers to...
options: conversation and cooperation between people of different religions
converting others to one's own faith
questions.explain: Inter-faith dialogue is respectful conversation and cooperation between different religions.

questions.q: In the study of religion, 'pluralism' is the view that...
options: only one religion is true and others are false
all major religions offer valid paths to the same ultimate truth
religion should be banned from public life
questions.explain: Pluralism sees the different religions as valid routes to the same ultimate reality.

questions.q: A believer who holds that salvation or truth is found only in their own religion is taking which position?
questions.explain: Exclusivism claims that truth or salvation is found only within one's own religion.

questions.q: Which statement best reflects an 'inclusivist' attitude towards other religions?
options: Only my religion is true; all others are wrong
All religions are equally valid and true
My religion holds the fullest truth, but other religions can contain some truth
Religion has no place in modern society
questions.explain: Inclusivism regards one's own faith as fullest but accepts partial truth in others.

questions.q: A Christian and a Muslim community hold a joint event to share food, discuss shared values and build understanding. This is an example of...
questions.explain: Shared events to build mutual understanding between religions are inter-faith dialogue.

questions.q: A humanist couple want a wedding that reflects their values without any reference to God. Which option best suits them?
options: A church wedding led by a priest
A humanist ceremony celebrating their commitment and shared human values
A pilgrimage to a holy site
questions.explain: A humanist ceremony marks commitment through shared human values without religious content.

questions.q: Which of the following is a benefit often associated with living in a multi-faith society?
options: greater religious conflict and less understanding
opportunities to learn from and respect a range of beliefs
the enforced practice of a single religion
the removal of all religion from public life
questions.explain: A multi-faith society allows people to learn from and respect diverse beliefs.

questions.q: A government decides that no single religion should control its laws, and people of all faiths and none are treated equally. This approach is an example of...
questions.explain: Keeping religion separate from the running of the state is secularism.

questions.q: The design (teleological) argument for God's existence claims that...
options: the universe must have a first cause
the order and complexity of the universe suggest a designer
the presence of evil shows God does not exist
questions.explain: The design argument infers a designer from the order and complexity of the universe.

questions.q: A student argues: 'If God is all-loving and all-powerful, why is there so much suffering in the world?' This challenge is known as...
questions.explain: Questioning how an all-loving, all-powerful God allows suffering is the problem of evil.

questions.q: Many religious believers today respond to the Big Bang theory by saying that...
options: God could have been the cause that brought about the Big Bang
religion and science can never be discussed together
questions.explain: Many believers see the Big Bang as the means by which God created the universe.
